UNIT 2 · STRATEGY VISIONING & SUCCESS IN PRACTICE (SiP)
Module 2 · Direction · Unit 2

UNIT INTENT
Before the organisation can define where it is going, leaders must agree on what strategy actually means, in the precise, strategic sense, translated to operational reality, that makes every subsequent decision coherent.
Three connected outputs carry the unit: the Strategy Architecture, the Strategy Intent Statement and Success in Practice. Protect the time in Section 4 for each group to build them in that order.
How the unit runs: Teach the whole unit from the deck first. Participants then go to the portal and complete their own page, in the session or after it.

Unit overview (facilitator file): This unit helps leaders to determine the organisation’s strategy architecture, articulate its strategic intent and define the Success in Practice (SiP) of the chosen Strategy Intent.

WHAT THE UNIT PRODUCES:
Each group builds three connected outputs, in this order.
1. The Strategy Architecture: the integrated strategic logic constructed from the 14 elements of the Strategy2Results® definition of strategy.
2. The Strategy Intent Statement: one crisp statement of strategic ambition derived from WHAT, WHY, HOW and WHEN.
3. Success in Practice (SiP): four confirmed statements, one for each SiP domain, read together as one picture of success.
The Architecture provides the logic. The Intent crystallises the ambition. Success in Practice makes the ambition observable.

HOW THE UNIT RUNS:
1. You teach the whole unit from this deck first, from Section 1 to the Unit Summary. The deck is the teaching material.
2. Participants then go to the portal and complete their own page, in the session or after it: the opening definition of strategy, the reflections, the three Section 4 outputs, the role contribution and the 5.2 observations.
3. Section 4 on the portal is group work. The group agrees each entry and one member acts as scribe. Every member then types the agreed entries into their own page.
4. Section 5 on the portal is individual work from an assigned executive role, followed by each group sharing with the room.
Each slide's notes end with a block headed "On the portal, after the teaching" wherever participants have something to complete for that part.

Your preparation as facilitator:
- Read the Facilitator Guide tab and every section of the facilitator file. 4.1 lists the 14 elements with the guide and the four questions each group sees. 4.3 lists the four SiP domains with the lead question and the three input questions.
- Confirm the groups and the assigned executive roles: CEO, CFO, COO, CHRO, CTO, CMO, CCO, CPO, CRO, CSO.
- Keep a whiteboard or flip chart for the opening definitions of strategy. You return to them at the Unit Summary.

Where the outputs go next:
- The three confirmed outputs feed the team's Capstone Blueprint. Its Unit 2 section opens once every member of the team has completed Unit 2.
- Unit 3 maps the Success in Practice through KISS and defines the OKRs that measure progress towards it.

Source detail (S2R® manuscript):

Module context: The Direction module (Strategy Intent & Direction Across Functions) equips participants to understand how each Executive Leadership role interprets strategic intent and direction, and the steps where these interpretations create cross-functional tension or reinforcement.
Participants work through the whole Direction module from the perspective of their assigned CXO role.

KEY LEARNING OUTCOMES 

1. Define strategy architecture and articulate strategic intent in relation to the organisation’s purpose, long-term value and stakeholder relevance.
2. Define a coherent future position and the organisational meaning of success.
3. Evaluate the consistency between strategic ambition, organisational identity and the realities of the operating environment.
4. Establish a shared strategic direction that supports consistent enterprise interpretation and decision-making.

HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:
Read the four outcomes aloud and say where the unit delivers each one.
- Outcome 1 is built in Section 1 (the definition and its architecture) and produced in 4.1 and 4.2 (the Strategy Architecture and the Strategy Intent Statement).
- Outcome 2 is built in 1.3 and Section 3 (the four SiP domains and their observable indicators) and produced in 4.3 (the four SiP statements).
- Outcome 3 is tested in 4.1, where each group checks that its choices reinforce one another and reflect the realities of its capability and environment, and in 3.2, where the SiP Flammables test the balance of the picture of success.
- Outcome 4 is built in Section 2 (the three functions the Strategy Intent and SiP serve) and applied in Section 5 (the contribution of each executive role).

Each section slide carries that section’s two learning outcomes.

QUESTION TO ASK:
"Which of these four outcomes would make the largest difference to how your leadership team works today?" 
Take two or three answers. They tell you where the room expects the most from the unit.

FACILITATOR GUIDE · SESSION OVERVIEW

HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:
1. Walk the five sections in one sentence each, using the list below.
2. Say plainly that Sections 1 to 3 prepare the thinking and Section 4 is where each group produces its three outputs. 
The Unit Intent asks you to protect the time for that work.
3. Tell participants how the unit runs: you teach all five sections from the deck first, and they then complete the unit on the portal, in the session or after it.

THE FIVE SECTIONS:
- Section 1 · Awareness — What: the Strategy2Results® definition of strategy, the Strategy Architecture underneath it, the Strategy Intent Statement and Success in Practice.

- Section 2 · Intelligence — Why: the three functions the Strategy Intent and SiP serve once they are defined: Strategic Alignment, Decision Filter and Execution Coherence.

- Section 3 · Extrapolating — Where: the observable indicators within each SiP domain, and the SiP Flammables that distort the picture of success.

- Section 4 · Integration — Collective: each group builds its Strategy Architecture, derives its Strategy Intent Statement and builds its Success in Practice.

- Section 5 · Application — In Practice: each participant applies the agreed Success in Practice to an executive role; the groups then share.
4:
SECTION 1 · AWARENESS — WHAT

HOW THIS SECTION RUNS:
1. Opening question: each participant writes a one-sentence definition of strategy 
2. 1.1: the Strategy2Results® definition of strategy and the nine concepts that make up the Strategy Architecture.
3. 1.2: the four dimensions that the Strategy Intent Statement brings forward from the architecture.
4. 1.3: Success in Practice and its four observable domains.
5. The Section 1 Reflections slide: the two reflections participants write on the portal after the teaching.

SECTION LEARNING OUTCOMES:
1. Redefine strategy to create a robust understanding of strategy architecture.
2. Distinguish the direction an organisation sets from the future position that defines its success.

FACILITATOR GUIDANCE — SECTION 1 · AWARENESS

SECTION INTENT: This section establishes the conceptual bedrock of the entire unit. 
Before any co-creation can happen, participants must share a single, precise definition of strategy and understand its three building blocks: the Strategy Architecture, the Strategy Intent Statement and Success in Practice.
